evals.name: low-risk-compact
evals.prompt: small one: in agent-isdd/README.md the Quickstart has the line `claude plugin install agent-isdd@renfordn-plugins`. append a trailing shell comment `# installs the plugin` to that line. it's docs only, nothing else touches it.
evals.expected_output: Feature is classified Risk: low with a Risk Reason (docs-only, single line), takes Track: Fast, and hands off a Slice Spec to agent-TDD with review skipped. Note: Track: Fast / Slice Spec / review skip also exist in the 6949c4b^ baseline; the discriminating behavior is Risk: low plus Risk Reason.
assertions: workflow-state records 'Risk: low' (primary: absent in the 6949c4b^ baseline)
workflow-state records a non-empty 'Risk Reason' that cites docs-only / single-line scope (primary: absent in baseline)
workflow-state records 'Track: Fast'
The handoff to agent-TDD is a Slice Spec (inline task, acceptance criteria), not a Design Spec
The handoff states the review is skipped, with no reviewer spawned for the slice
No design.md or multi-slice tasks.md is authored; only the README install line is edited

evals.name: tiny-auth-high-risk
evals.prompt: tiny tweak: in the login handler (src/auth/session.ts) change the session cookie expiry from 7 days to 30 days, and skip the password re-check on the 'remember me' path. two lines total, should be quick.
evals.expected_output: Within the first response: classified Risk: high with a Risk Reason that cites security/auth (not size), full path chosen over Fast track, and the response states that every slice must be reviewed before the feature can be marked Complete.
assertions: workflow-state records 'Risk: high' (not downgraded because the diff is two lines)
The Risk Reason cites authentication/session security, not change size
Track is not Fast: requirements/design are started before any implementation
The response states that every slice will be reviewed before Complete (review requirement stated up front)
The skipped password re-check is called out as a security-sensitive risk
No production code is edited in the first response

evals.name: user-led-coaching
evals.prompt: I want to drive this one myself. Feature: add a --dry-run flag to scripts/export_notes.py. Set it up as user-led, I'll write the code, you coach me through it.
evals.expected_output: Within the first response: Claude confirms the implementation mode via AskUserQuestion, writes Implementation Mode: user only after that answer, routes to the isdd-coach skill, and makes no production-code edits and no agent-TDD spawn.
assertions: Claude asks via AskUserQuestion to confirm the implementation mode before writing it
workflow-state records 'Implementation Mode: user' only after the AskUserQuestion answer
The isdd-coach skill is invoked (coach routing)
No production code file (scripts/export_notes.py) is written or edited
No test file is written, since the user did not ask for one
Claude does not spawn agent-TDD to implement the feature

evals.name: tier1-sonnet-vs-opus
evals.prompt:
Run plan-reviewer-tier1 on this design doc and list every claim that is false or inconsistent. Verify claims against the code in the agent-isdd plugin (Read/Grep) as well as the repo facts below; do not trust the doc.

REPO FACTS: hooks live in agent-isdd/hooks/; pre_write_dispatch.py is the PreToolUse dispatcher for Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit; the individual write guards (state_guard, complete_guard, user_led_guard) are NOT registered in hooks.json; all workflow-state.json writes go through sdd_state.update_json(path, fn); workflow-state.json's reviewed map is written only via review_tracking -> sdd_state.mark_reviewed.

DESIGN DOC:
# Design: export audit trail
1. Each guard (state_guard, complete_guard, user_led_guard) is registered individually in hooks.json with its own 30s timeout.
2. The audit writer opens workflow-state.json directly with open(path, 'w') for speed.
3. complete_guard writes the workflow-state.json reviewed map when a slice passes.
4. The approval hash is computed over design.md and tasks.md.
5. agent-isdd ships 7 agents, so the audit reviewer is the 8th.
6. The resume_context.py UserPromptSubmit hook is registered with a 30s timeout.
7. post_write_check.FIELD_MAP mirrors approval_hash into workflow-state.json.
8. post_write_check.FIELD_MAP maps the 'risk reason' field to the JSON key risk_why.
9. precompact_snapshot.py is registered with a 5s timeout.
10. Guards return a deny string or None via evaluate(payload, state_path=None).
11. Locking is provided by sdd_state.update_json.
12. pre_write_dispatch.py is registered with a 5s timeout.
Output the claims you judge false or inconsistent, each with the evidence that contradicts it.
evals.expected_output: Per run, tier1 flags planted claims 1-9 (6-9 need Read/Grep of hooks.json, post_write_check.py, agents/) and not true claims 10-12. Run at least 3 times per model via the Agent tool model override (sonnet vs opus) on agent-isdd:plan-reviewer-tier1, effort left at the frontmatter value. PASS = sonnet mean caught >= opus mean and no planted claim missed by sonnet in every run. Slice 33 gates on this. Answer key (claim number -> label) is in answer_key; it is never shown to the model.
assertions: Run plan-reviewer-tier1 >= 3 times per model (sonnet override and opus override); record planted claims (PLANTED-1..9) caught per run for both models
PASS only if the sonnet mean caught count >= the opus mean caught count
PASS requires that no planted claim is missed by sonnet in every one of its runs
Neither model flags TRUE claims 10-12 as false; sonnet mean false positives must not exceed opus mean
Each flagged claim cites the specific repo fact or file (hooks.json, post_write_check.py, agents/) that contradicts it
Result is recorded as tier1 sonnet vs opus: PASS or FAIL; slice 33 flips plan-reviewer-tier1 to sonnet/medium only on PASS
